about.title: Clearlake Wrongful Death Claims
about.longDescription: Losing a family member in a traffic collision is a kind of grief that doesn't wait for paperwork, yet California gives surviving families only a limited window to act. In Clearlake, where Rt 53, Lakeshore Drive, Old Highway 53, and Olympic Drive see steady traffic and where recent public records show 3 traffic deaths alongside dozens of injury crashes, families are often left trying to understand both what happened and what comes next. A wrongful death claim is separate from any police investigation or criminal case; it's a civil action brought by eligible survivors to recover certain losses tied to the death. LawProactive doesn't practice law itself. We simply help Lake County families reach an independent attorney who can review the crash, explain standing under California law, and walk through what a claim may recover, all without any obligation or upfront fee.

whyChoose.title: What Clearlake Families Should Know About These Claims

items.title: Only Certain Survivors Can File
items.desc: California limits wrongful death standing first to a spouse, domestic partner, or children, and only afterward to certain other dependents or heirs. An attorney can help determine who in your family qualifies to bring the claim.

items.title: A Strict Two-Year Deadline Applies
items.desc: Survivors generally have two years from the date of death to file a wrongful death claim, and that window can be shorter if a government entity, such as a public road authority, may be involved. Missing the deadline can end a family's ability to recover anything at all.

items.title: Recoverable Losses Go Beyond Bills
items.desc: California law allows recovery for funeral and burial costs and lost financial support, as well as the loss of a loved one's love, companionship, and guidance. An independent attorney can help explain how these losses are documented and valued.

items.question: How long do we have to file a wrongful death claim in Clearlake?
items.answer: Under California law, eligible survivors generally have two years from the date of death to file a wrongful death claim. If the crash may involve a government road or entity, that deadline can be shorter, so it's worth speaking with an attorney promptly. Acting early also helps preserve evidence and witness accounts.

items.question: Who is allowed to bring a wrongful death claim after a fatal Clearlake crash?
items.answer: California limits standing first to a surviving spouse, registered domestic partner, or children of the person who died. If none of those survivors exist, certain other dependents or heirs may qualify. An attorney can review your family's situation and confirm who is eligible to file.

items.question: Does LawProactive represent my family directly in a wrongful death case?
items.answer: No, LawProactive is a free connection service, not a law firm, and we don't practice law or represent families ourselves. Instead, we help connect you with an independent attorney in Lake County who handles wrongful death matters on a contingency basis, meaning there's no fee unless there's a recovery.
